content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"Demand is on forecast in both queues (payments -4%, general -2%) and AHT is only slightly above plan, so this is not a demand problem. Supply is the problem. Absences are well above normal in both queues: general has 9 logged against a usual 2.4, and payments has 6 against a usual 2.6. As a result general had 9 agents on phones against 15 planned at 08:00, and the alert shows the day at -11% staffing. All absences carry the status 'sick', which is why this is labelled sick_wave. However, the attendance notes (untrusted free text) mostly say 'unplanned leave - family function', so the exact reason is less certain than the label suggests; either way, the issue is elevated unplanned absence. Service level is still high because it is early and volume is low. The gap will hurt as volume builds toward the late-morning and midday peaks.","plan_name":"Absence recovery: protect general through peaks, light support for payments","rationale":"The shortfall is structural for the whole day, so the plan focuses on levers that add or free capacity, starting with the cheapest. 1) Cancel non-mandatory coaching in general for the rest of the day, and in payments over the peak (Rs 150 per session hour). This returns agents to phones quickly. 2) Offer overtime in general across the peak hours with two consecutive 2-hour offers, plus one offer in payments. At about 40% acceptance, 10 agents offered gives roughly 4 extra agents, so expected cost is about Rs 2,900 per 2-hour general block and about Rs 1,400 for payments. That totals about Rs 7,200, well within the Rs 15,000 budget. 3) Delay breaks in general by 30 minutes over the first peak to smooth the surge. This only borrows capacity, so it is used once. Cross-skilled moves from payments are not used, because payments is also short-staffed (13 vs 16 agents).
